background_notes.fact: If a complex vector space V has finite dimension n and a family indexed by J is a complex basis of V, then J is finite of cardinal n. If the same family is an integer basis of M, any bijection Fin(n)→J reindexes both bases simultaneously.

background_notes.justification: The finite exchange argument bounds every independent family by the size of a finite basis. For completeness, expand a fixed n-element basis in the given basis; the union of these finite supports spans V and independence forces every given basis vector into that union. Both bases are now finite, and exchange in both directions makes their cardinalities equal to n. Transport along a bijection of their index sets preserves expansion uniqueness over both scalar rings.

background_notes.fact: Every field satisfies the strong rank condition. A basis indexed by a finite nonempty set spans a finite-dimensional nonzero vector space, and no member of that basis is zero.

grounds.reason: F001 gives n>0 and the I-indexed basis b.
I=Fin(n) is finite and contains 0 when n>0.

background_notes.justification: For a surjection K^a→K^b, the images of the a coordinate vectors span K^b; finite exchange gives b≤a, the strong rank condition required by M006. A finite basis is a finite spanning family, hence gives finite-dimensionality. If β_0 were zero, the finite relation with coefficient 1 at 0 and 0 elsewhere would violate independence since 1≠0 in a field.
